video_title: Do Wemby, Spurs Have MOMENTUM In Series???

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Mitch Johnson's coaching adjustments and lineup changes in Game 3
quotes.excerpt: I love the idea that such a young coach in Mitch Johnson just had the goal to do that.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: I love the idea that such a young coach in Mitch Johnson just had the goal to do that. To make the switch after failing, giving up fourth-quarter leads in Game 1 and Game 2, he went with what works the first three quarters. I like having that lineup on the floor. They are smaller, they are versatile. When you have a 7'6" guy to cover the paint, you don't really need a natural power forward or a small forward. When you have a guy like Stephon Castle that plays a lot bigger than his size and Victor Wembanyama, you can afford to play De'Aaron Fox and Dylan Harper at the same time.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: No matter what the position is, I got to put five guys out on the floor that's going to give me the best chance to win the game. And what Chandler just said, Dylan Harper didn't shoot it great from the field, but he rebounded better than the other guards in the game where the possessions matter so much. You got to keep a 6'5" rebounding guard in there. He almost had a double-double with nine rebounds and what he was able to do on the field. So you got to give him a chance.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: The Spurs' aggressive playstyle and veteran leadership from De'Aaron Fox
quotes.excerpt: It was the aggressiveness, it was the fact that all three guys are a threat anytime the ball is in their hands.
quotes.quote: It was the aggressiveness, it was the fact that all three guys are a threat anytime the ball is in their hands. Lou made a really good point as far as we have to realize when it comes to De'Aaron Fox and his struggles, this is only his second playoff appearance. And obviously, he is that veteran guy that was brought in to kind of keep the ship afloat when the water got a little rough. He did exactly that last night. The numbers aren't jumping off the page, but he does his job as that veteran, and that's something that doesn't show up on the stat line. I think all three guys were clicking, especially when it came to the aggressiveness, and I think that's what changed the game.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: The value of De'Aaron Fox's contract in the NBA Finals
quotes.excerpt: If the Knicks win, of course he has, who cares? It proved to be right.
quotes.quote: We were talking yesterday, is Mikal Bridges worth the five picks? If the Knicks win, of course he has, who cares? It proved to be right. It's the same thing with De'Aaron Fox and that salary. That salary seems real bad right now because they have Dylan Harper that's on a rookie deal for the next two or three years, and he's kind of on his ass. He's going to take his playing time and he's going to take his starting position. But they are in the NBA Finals. If they happen to win this championship, does it really matter that they are paying this dude? Obviously, they would like to make some adjustments, but it's the same thing with Mikal Bridges. These are the two best teams left in the NBA with that trade and with that contract.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of locker room culture on playing struggling veterans
quotes.excerpt: It depends on what kind of locker room you in. If you in a toxic locker room and he's not producing, you might have guys looking around like...
quotes.quote: It depends on what kind of locker room you in. If you in a toxic locker room and he's not producing, you might have guys looking around like, 'I got to be getting paid next.' If that's what you giving, if you're in those type of locker rooms. But if you understand that you pay a guy what he qualifies for, De'Aaron Fox qualifies for that type of money and he's that caliber player. Now, struggles aside, he's no different than anybody else. Guys are allowed to struggle. Every time they do struggle, the reality is we're going to put your contract and your money as one of those things that's a forefront.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: De'Aaron Fox's performance and role on a balanced Spurs team
quotes.excerpt: He fit in beautifully for during the most of the the season.
quotes.quote: We are talking about a guy that averaged 19, 6, and 4 in 72 games this year. It's not like he had an awful season. Remember there were questions, what are they going to do with all the depth at guard and how are they going to fit in De'Aaron Fox? He fit in beautifully for during the most of the the season. He was their closer at times in the end of game in the fourth quarter. So yes, he struggled, yes his ankle I don't think is 100%, that's part of it, everyone goes through that. And naturally, you do get higher expectations when you make that kind of money. There is a level of expectations and it's the nature of the beast in the game and free agency.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Dylan Harper's impact on the Spurs' success
quotes.excerpt: I don't even think we're having this conversation if Dylan Harper isn't having the impact that he's having.
quotes.quote: I don't even think we're having this conversation if Dylan Harper isn't having the impact that he's having. I think that's a big part of why we're even having this conversation. Other than that, I think it'd be water under the bridge. And he's the future, so it's like, damn, why are we paying this dude this much money when we got a player just as good that could possibly will be better as early as next year? That's where the conversation comes in.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: De'Aaron Fox's role as a veteran learning during the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: So is it making excuses to say, you know, this could be a veteran that's still learning at the same time?
quotes.quote: So is it making excuses to say, you know, this could be a veteran that's still learning at the same time? Still figuring the game out, figuring out the playoffs? Like we said, this is a guy that's only had one playoff run before this one. He helped me win a game last night. That was a big shot.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: The rising financial expectations for De'Aaron Fox
quotes.excerpt: 54 million next year, 57, 28 and 62 in the last year.
quotes.quote: 54 million next year, 57, 28 and 62 in the last year. So that's where the conversations are only going to get louder. But they are, again, they're winning. They're in the finals. They're in the finals. Who cares? Like this is what you you pay guys to win championships. Maybe he's one of the worst contracts on that team, but they're still in a position to win a championship with that salary. It's impressive.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: De'Aaron Fox needs to play faster to maximize his strengths
quotes.excerpt: I would like to see him play a little faster.
quotes.quote: I would like to see him play a little faster. You know, I think that's one of his strengths when it comes to breaking down his game. And I see a lot of the times, you know, in random play where he's kind of walking the ball up or or tiptoeing up the court. I think, you know, him pushing the ball in those moments, uh getting to the cup, I think, I think we'll see better performances and a better stat line at the end of the game. So I would like to see him play to his strengths a little more.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: The Spurs' team dynamic and De'Aaron Fox's off-ball role
quotes.excerpt: We're used to seeing De'Aaron Fox being a ball dominant guard bringing it up, creating in transition.
quotes.quote: And he got to have the ball in his hands. Like we're used to seeing De'Aaron Fox being a ball dominant guard bringing it up, creating in transition, playing faster like like Boogie just said. But you're dealing with a different dynamic of a team. You got a 7'5" guy that's getting the rebound, he's pushing the ball up the floor. If Dylan Harper gets the ball, he's going to push it up the floor. They trust Stephon Castle in the open floor with the ball. Nobody's waiting around, outletting the ball to just De'Aaron Fox. So that's putting him in a position where he's playing kind of like a two or he's playing like a three because he's off-ball so much. So it can be a period of adjustment for him as well just as anybody else and that's kind of where you're seeing the numbers get a little wacky.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: The Spurs' high-speed offense and De'Aaron Fox's role
quotes.excerpt: When I see Harper, when I see Castle and they play in the open floor, they're playing with a lot of speed.
quotes.quote: Man, but I I agree as far as that part where it's obviously other guys touching the ball, but when I see Harper, when I see Castle and they play in the open floor, they're playing with a lot of speed. They're they're pushing the rock. So I'm expecting the same thing from De'Aaron Fox. And on top of that, if you do have two other guys on the floor that's able to create that type of gravity, it's open shots for everybody. We've we've also seen him catch on outside, pump fake nobody and drive nowhere.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: The need for De'Aaron Fox to be an impactful shooter
quotes.excerpt: That 0 for 5 from 3, that got to turn into a 3 for 5 or a 2 for 5.
quotes.quote: And that's where the adjustment come in. That's why that 0 for 5 from 3, that got to turn into a 3 for 5 or a 2 for 5 or somewhere where you are where you are impactful, because if them guys going to continue to get downhill, you got to be a threat if they going to kick the ball out to us. So I'm with you on that.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: The Spurs' resilience despite being down 2-0 in the series
quotes.excerpt: We haven't played good and when we watched the film, we realized that we are okay being down 0-2.
quotes.quote: Stephon Castle said postgame which I I took right to heart. He said, 'We haven't played good and when we watched the film, we realized that we are okay being down 0-2 right now.' Because think about it, they were up 13, they smoked the lead. Castle had that crazy burst where he was all over the glass and kind of willed the Knicks back. And that was more they let one go, but the Knicks really played well down the stretch. Outside of one inadvertent turnover and mishap and a foul in Game 2, again, this whole series shifts. And it sounds crazy and silly to say they could be up 3-0, but they really are in the worst shape ever being down 2-1.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons' confidence in the Spurs heading into Game 4
quotes.excerpt: I'm have the utmost confidence right now if on the Spurs going into Game 4.
quotes.quote: I'm have the utmost confidence right now if on the Spurs going into Game 4 knowing that I've been in every single ball game and we blew it. They didn't win, we lost is how I'm thinking about if on the Spurs.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: The Spurs' resilience in overcoming double-digit leads
quotes.excerpt: Three straight games, they've blown double-digit leads.
quotes.quote: Three straight games, they've blown double-digit leads. And they're up 13 and they were one one turnover with tie game like like I feel good about I feel like I'm a part of the game. You're up 13, so you hold up, you're up 13 and you get it back down to a one-possession game again. Again, and you feel like you're the better team? I don't understand the logic. You got to break that down.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons' belief in the Spurs' talent and depth
quotes.excerpt: First of all, my body of work, my season, I I've had like I'm talent, depth.
quotes.quote: First of all, my body of work, my season, I I've had like I'm talent, depth, like everything across the board, I think the Spurs are better.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: The Spurs' need to focus on the NBA Finals
quotes.excerpt: Let's start at the finals.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons' analysis of the Spurs' performance in Game 1 and 2
quotes.excerpt: I have played well enough in the first two games that we lost to have won the game.
quotes.quote: I am just saying I have played well enough in the first two games that we lost to have won the game. Especially that Game 1, if they took they took their foot off the gas and again, we talk about the inexperience, all this stuff that maybe have caused that. Game 2, again, that's just a bad turnover by Victor Wembanyama and a bad foul. Without that and again, Sean Elliott said one play doesn't determine the outcome of the game, but that was a big play.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: The Spurs' need for better performances from key players
quotes.excerpt: We still haven't seen a great game from Jalen Brunson.
quotes.quote: We still haven't seen a great game from Jalen Brunson. Mikal Bridges, he had one great game. He hasn't been who he is. OG has been great, Cat has been great, the Knicks bench has been outplaying their second group this entire time. So some of those things I'm not I'm not really rolling with. I think you can make a case for both of these teams. I think it's a heavyweight fight and the Spurs got involved a little late.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams' prediction for a breakout game in the series
quotes.excerpt: If you ask me which one of these teams is is going to have a breakout game before the other, I still feel like it's the Knicks.
quotes.quote: If you ask me which one of these teams is is going to have a breakout game before the other, I still feel like it's the Knicks.
